extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Hertz Foundation Fellowship (U.S. citizens or permanent residents) and their recommenders
extracted.subtask_description: FAQ and application rules for submitting a Hertz Fellowship application, including eligibility, required materials, recommenders, deadlines, participating-school policies, and evaluation expectations for essays and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and key dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 Fellowship application will open on August 28, 2025, and close on Friday, October 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM PST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note these firm application opening and closing dates and times. (See separate entries for recommender deadline and interview timeline.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview selection process and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: After the application closes, applicants who advance beyond pre-selection will be invited to first round interviews (via Zoom). First round interviews occur in December and January; second round in-person interviews for select finalists take place in February. Fellows selected in late March will be notified in April and announced publicly in May; funding begins in the fall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should hear about application status by late November for pre-selection. Plan availability for potential Zoom interviews in December/January and in-person travel in February if selected as a finalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — academic stage and fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be college seniors, first-year graduate students, or individuals in a gap year preparing to apply to graduate school, who intend to pursue a PhD in the applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics, or engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when you are a senior, in a gap year before starting graduate school, or in the first year of graduate study; the program funds individuals pursuing a PhD in the listed fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship/permanent residency and moral commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of the United States. Applicants who are not yet citizens will be asked for proof of Application for Citizenship or their Permanent Resident card if they advance to the interview phase. Applicants are asked to make a moral commitment to make their skills available to the United States in times of national emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-citizen/permanent-resident applicants should be prepared to document immigration status if selected to interview. The Foundation expects a stated moral commitment to serve the U.S. in emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD/PhD eligibility and funding scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hertz Fellowship will fund only the PhD portion of an MD/PhD program. MD/PhD students are encouraged to apply during the year before starting the PhD portion or during their first year of the PhD portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are an MD/PhD student, apply in the year you will begin your PhD research (or during the first PhD year); note fellowship funds only the PhD portion. MD/PhD students who never took the GRE may submit MCAT scores in place of GRE scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-time enrollment and participating-school requirement for funding
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive fellowship funding, students must be enrolled full-time in one of the Hertz Foundation’s approved participating schools. Fellows may request their school be added if it is not listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may apply whether or not you currently attend a participating school. If awarded and your school is not on the list, you may petition to have it added; Fellows may transfer to another participating school during the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating schools list and application policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation has a defined list of participating U.S. institutions with which it coordinates paying stipend, tuition, and other costs (9-month stipend model). Applicants do not need to be enrolled at or nominated by a participating school to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full list of participating schools is provided. If awarded, you can request a school be added or transfer to a different participating school as needed; the Foundation will evaluate requested schools for U.S. location and academic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload transcripts using the online application. Unofficial transcripts are accepted for the initial application; official transcripts will be requested if selected as a finalist. If graduate transcripts are not yet available for first-year graduate students, only undergraduate transcripts are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only provide graduate transcripts if grades have been posted; otherwise submit undergrad transcripts. Use the online system to upload documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper-division course reporting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Every university defines upper-division courses somewhat differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your best judgment to identify and detail courses you consider upper-division when asked on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay length guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are less concerned with exact word length and more with the applicant’s ability to adequately address prompts. Suggested lengths: 250–500 words for various short essays and 500–1000 words for the Personal Essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may go under or over suggested lengths; prioritize fully answering the prompt and demonstrating fit rather than strict adherence to word counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal essay evaluation focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation looks for personal essays that reveal your creativity beyond your research — e.g., favorite extracurricular activities, leadership experiences, or other information that helps the reviewers understand who you are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the personal essay to show dimensions of creativity, character, and interests that are not captured by research summaries alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document upload limits and file handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The application allows uploading multiple documents. Please limit the size to five megabytes per document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each uploaded file is ≤5 MB; combine or compress materials as necessary to meet the per-document size limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference/recommender requirements — format and number
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must register four references in the online application. All references must complete the Foundation’s specific evaluation form that is emailed to them; supplemental letters in other formats are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation uses a structured evaluation form (with specific questions and checkbox items) because it yields information needed for review; do not ask recommenders to submit free-form letters outside the provided form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender evaluation content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference form asks recommenders to highlight notable examples of personal creativity in the applicant’s work, the applicant’s strengths and weaknesses at their current stage of training, discussion of potential as an applied scientist or engineer, and comparisons to other students at the same stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose recommenders who can speak specifically about your scientific knowledge, creativity, potential as an applied scientist/engineer, and provide comparative assessments to peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing recommenders and applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing recommenders, select those familiar with your scientific knowledge and who can provide examples of creativity. Applicants should be proactive in requesting recommenders complete the evaluation form and allocate enough time for them to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform recommenders that they will receive a questionnaire form (not a standard letter) and that the Foundation learns more through these specific questions; remind them and check that they received the email (including spam folder).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender submission deadline and late-submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline for recommender evaluations is Monday, November 3rd at 6:00 p.m. Pacific. The Foundation provides a buffer between the application deadline (October 31) and the recommender deadline (November 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only references submitted by the recommender deadline are guaranteed to be included in reviewer files. The Foundation will not accept recommenders’ completed evaluations after the recommender deadline for guaranteed inclusion; applications will still be reviewed even if some letters are missing. Contact fellowshipinfo@hertzfoundation.org with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRE policy and score handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRE is optional. GRE Subject Test scores are accepted but not required. Scores may be submitted after the application deadline; if not received by initial interview decisions, files will be reviewed without them. MD/PhD students may submit MCAT scores in place of GRE if they never took the GRE. Previously sent ETS scores are retained unless you have new scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose to submit GRE scores, use the Foundation’s code #4366. Submitting GRE scores after the application deadline is permitted, but may not be considered for early interview decisions if not received in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement to submit a proposed research project. The fellowship is intended to fund individual students, not a specific project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application does provide opportunities to summarize current and prior research experiences and interests you intend to pursue; focus on your intellectual trajectory rather than a fixed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent awards, coordination, and deferral policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If awarded both a Hertz fellowship and another fellowship, scholarship or grant, you do not need to decline the other award. The Foundation coordinates with entities like NSF, NIH, and NDSEG to enable recipients to take advantage of multiple awards and receive maximum compensation. You may also defer your Hertz fellowship for other grants or scholarships (e.g., Fulbright, Rhodes, Churchill, Marshall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify the Foundation and coordinate to maximize combined benefits; deferral requests are possible for major awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who are not offered a fellowship may reapply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reapplying, demonstrate clear progress and development since the previous application to strengthen your candidacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship benefits, duration, and stipend model
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hertz Fellowship awards up to five years of funding, valued at up to $250,000. The Foundation coordinates stipend, tuition, and other costs via a 9-month stipend model with participating schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If awarded, your stipend and financial arrangements will be coordinated through the agreement the Foundation maintains with participating institutions; understand the 9-month stipend structure when planning finances.
